_description: Fixture 1 — Climate Change baseline. Well-supported claims with clear evidence. No contradictions.
research_question: What are the primary drivers of global average temperature increase since 1850?

report.executive_summary: Global average temperatures have risen approximately 1.1°C since pre-industrial times, driven primarily by greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel combustion and deforestation. [SOURCE 1] Scientific consensus on anthropogenic climate change is overwhelming. [SOURCE 2]
key_findings: CO2 concentrations have increased from 280 ppm pre-industrial to over 420 ppm in 2023. [SOURCE 1]
The 2011–2020 decade was the warmest on record according to WMO data. [SOURCE 2]
Deforestation contributes approximately 10% of annual global greenhouse gas emissions. [SOURCE 3]
Methane emissions from agriculture and livestock account for 14.5% of global emissions. [SOURCE 4]
report.limitations: Temperature records before 1850 rely on proxy data with higher uncertainty.

evidence.content: Atmospheric CO2 concentration reached 421 ppm in May 2023, the highest in over 800,000 years of ice core records. Pre-industrial baseline was approximately 280 ppm.
The 2011–2020 decade was the warmest decade ever recorded globally, with a global mean temperature 1.1°C above the pre-industrial (1850–1900) period. (WMO Global Climate Report 2020)
Land-use change including deforestation accounts for approximately 10–12% of total annual anthropogenic CO2-equivalent emissions according to IPCC AR6.

Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) emissions, of which livestock enteric fermentation is the largest component, contribute 14.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. (FAO 2013 Tackling Climate Change Through Livestock)
